self.neutral: The speaker's delivery is factual, flat, or carries no clear emotion; also use this when the line is too short or ambiguous to tell.
self.joy: The speaker sounds happy, amused, grateful, excited, or is celebrating.
self.anger: The speaker sounds angry, irritated, frustrated, or indignant.
self.sadness: The speaker sounds sad, disappointed, lonely, or hurt.
self.surprise: The speaker sounds astonished, amazed, or caught off guard.
self.fear: The speaker sounds afraid, anxious, or alarmed.
self.disgust: The speaker sounds disgusted, repulsed, or contemptuous.

listening.neutral: The listener has no clear reason to react visibly; also use this when the line is small talk or too ambiguous to react to.
listening.joy: The listener would look pleased, amused, or glad at what was just said.
listening.anger: The listener would look angry, irritated, or offended by what was just said.
listening.sadness: The listener would look saddened, disappointed, or hurt by what was just said.
listening.surprise: The listener would look startled or taken aback by what was just said.
listening.fear: The listener would look alarmed or worried by what was just said.
listening.disgust: The listener would look disgusted or repelled by what was just said.
